title: chore(deps): resolve @objectstack/* 17.7.0; attach the objectui#11334 mirror and objectui#11417's arm, follow 17.7.0's mechanical moves; the eager-closure line raised on maintainer ruling A (objectui#11717)
body:
Fixes #11717
Fixes #11334
Fixes #11417
Clause-②: yes — measured, see "Clause ②" below. The claim (`6019218018`) said `no` and delegated the answer to this measurement.

## What this PR is

`pnpm-lock.yaml` now resolves `@objectstack/*` 17.7.0. It was regenerated with pnpm only, never edited by hand. Every gate the bump turned red is listed below by row. The card's three riders ride here: the objectui#11334 mirror, objectui#11417's single-series arm, and the objectui#11624 `sortField` flips. One gate went red that was not mechanical: `check:eager-closure`. Maintainer ruling A (`6027998226`) resolved it, and the raise is one commit on this branch, `b680973f`. See "Resolved by ruling A" below.

| package | before (`main` lock) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `@objectstack/spec` · `types` · `core` · `client` · `formula` · `lint` · `sdui-parser` | 17.6.0 | 17.7.0 |

Nothing else moved. The census of package and snapshot keys runs in both directions: seven keys removed at 17.6.0 and seven added at 17.7.0, the same for the peer-context keys. The only importer `specifier` lines that move are the two floors below.

**How the lock was regenerated.** I used the route of the 17.5.0 and 17.6.0 bumps. Every `@objectstack/*` specifier was raised to `^17.7.0` for one `pnpm install`. Every manifest was then restored byte for byte to HEAD, and a second `pnpm install` reconciled the importers. `main` moved by ten commits while this was in flight, including objectui#11686's lockfile edit. I merged it as a merge commit, not a rebase, and git merged the lockfile without a conflict. After the merge, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` exited 0 with engine-strict on, and a plain `pnpm install` left the lockfile byte-identical. For round 2, `main` had moved 13 more commits. I merged `9b673e54` as a second merge commit, `c1e32e96`, again not a rebase, and git merged it without a conflict, the lockfile included. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` exited 0 on that head, and it exited 0 again on `b680973f`. The 43 test files the merge brought in ran green against 17.7.0 under the lock (376 tests), so the merge brought no new red to fix.

**Floors.** Two move, each because published code now imports something an older release does not export. `check:spec-floors` is green over a full build.
- `@object-ui/types`: `^17.6.0` to `^17.7.0`. It now chains `checkDashboardWidgetChartMeasureArity` and `checkPageRequiresKind`, which 17.7.0 first exports.
- `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard`: `^17.5.0` to `^17.6.0`. `DatasetWidget` now reads `DASHBOARD_WIDGET_MULTI_MEASURE_TYPES`, which 17.6.0 first exports (objectstack `11d28c17`; the ancestry reading is below).

## The card's riders

- **objectui#11334, the mirror.** `DashboardWidgetSchema` chains `.superRefine(checkDashboardWidgetChartMeasureArity)` after the metric-family chain, by import, with no second copy of the check. The 7715 census names it. Its `notAttachable` booking and both `OWED_TO_OBJECTUI_11334` ledgers (the types 8894 file and the panel 8894 file) are struck by flipping their rows to the refusal; no assertion was deleted. The cap rows now require the unrefused set to be EMPTY. The arms are read off the exported check itself. The dimensionless two-measure `pie` is pinned on both faces as ONE issue at `values` with the spec's own message.
  - ⚠️ The ruling asks for the one-dimension `pie` as the parse control. 17.7.0 refuses that `pie` anyway, through the single-series arm. So the control is stated per arm: with one dimension the dimensionless refusal is gone, the refusal that remains is the single-series one, and a two-measure `radar` with one dimension parses on both faces.
- **objectui#11417, the single-series arm.** Each of the arm's types (read off the check: `pie`, `donut`, `funnel`, `treemap`, `sankey`) is pinned refused with one dimension and two measures, on both faces, with the spec's own issue. Two controls: one measure with a dimension parses, and `scatter` / `radar` with a dimension and two measures parse. PR objectui#11433's two door assertions flip to the stored-document form. `MEASURE_AXIS_CHART_FAMILIES` is now `new Set(DASHBOARD_WIDGET_MULTI_MEASURE_TYPES)`, read off `CHART_TYPE_MAP` exactly as before (`table` / `pivot` are no `CHART_TYPE_MAP` family and keep `isTable`), so what is drawn does not change. Its remaining items are done here, so this PR completes the card.
- **objectui#11624's `sortField` rows.** `object-master-detail-form-details-entry-11396`'s forward tripwire flips to REFUSED on both published faces, with the spec's retired-key message at the member. The prose moves in the five places the card lists: the `MasterDetailDetailConfig` docblock, the 8071 test's header and compile-time block, the types pin's header, the `details` registration description, and the console parity row. `MasterDetailDetailConfig` keeps its `Omit`, because the 17.7.0 entry still LISTS the key as a tombstone.

### Resolved by ruling A (`6027998226`)

`check:eager-closure` (CI `Bundle Analysis`) was the one red that was not mechanical. The maintainer answered decision request `6024630321` with ruling A, record `6027998226` on objectui#11717. The selection, verbatim: 「A 抬预算+回收卡 (Recommended)」. One commit, `b680973f`, raises the line in the objectui#11088 shape:

| constant | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `BASELINE` | 3,386,193 over 330 of 2450 chunks, `2ba091c` | 3,591,028 over 331 of 2451 chunks, `c1e32e96` |
| `MAX_EAGER_CLOSURE_GZIP_BYTES` | 3,410,284 | 3,637,000 |
| `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE['vendor-objectstack']` | 1,420,958 | 1,604,474 |
| `PER_CHUNK_GZIP_CEILINGS['vendor-objectstack']` | 1,439,157 | 1,623,000 |

- The new ceiling is 3,591,028 + 45,568 (half of `REGRESSION_THIS_GATE_MUST_CATCH_BYTES`) = 3,636,596, rounded to the nearest thousand as every earlier raise was. That leaves 45,972 bytes of headroom, 0.50x.
- The new `vendor-objectstack` ceiling leaves 18,526 bytes of headroom, 0.20x, the band the two paybacks kept.
- `REGRESSION_THIS_GATE_MUST_CATCH_BYTES` is untouched. No exemption was added, and no import was made lazy.
- The other three per-chunk rows passed on this build and did not move.

The bytes, in gzip bytes. The instrument is the same for both columns: `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter=!@object-ui/site --concurrency=2` under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, in one container, then `pnpm check:eager-closure`, which reads `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json`. The control is `main` `9b673e54`, built in a worktree of its own with 17.6.0 resolved.

| chunk | `9b673e54` (`main`) | `c1e32e96` (merged head) | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|

| `ui-components` | 283,061 | 283,079 | +18 |

What the bytes buy: the console's client-side validation answers as the 17.7.0 server does, with its new refusals and its schemas. They also unblock the cards this bump unblocks. They do not buy a new console capability.

The payback card is objectstack#22044. When it lands, the ceiling and `BASELINE` come down together by exactly what it recovers, the way objectui#11101 and objectui#11438 lowered the third raise.

The gate's header has a new section, "⚠️ RAISED A FOURTH TIME, ON EXPLICIT MAINTAINER RULING (objectui#11717)". It carries the ruling, this table, the instrument and the payback card. On `b680973f`, `pnpm check:eager-closure` exits 0 and prints: "Console eager closure is 3506.9 KB gzipped across 331 of 2451 chunks (budget: 3551.8 KB, headroom: 44.9 KB)", aggregate 0.50x, `vendor-objectstack` 1566.9 KB against a 1585.0 KB ceiling (0.20x).

## Clause ②

This was measured on the built declaration closure of `@object-ui/types`. Its `dist` was built at `main` `7300fca` (spec 17.6.0, a worktree of its own) and at this branch (17.7.0), and the `.d.ts` files were compared with comment lines dropped and line order ignored:
- Nine files differ only in docblock text or ordering.
- Four differ in declarations: `zod/index.zod.d.ts`, `zod/objectql.zod.d.ts`, `zod/public-blocks.zod.d.ts` and `zod/layout.zod.d.ts`.

The emitted zod declarations inline the spec's shapes, so the bump moves what `@object-ui/types` publishes in both directions:
- members are typed where they were records of unknown values (the `action:group` / `action:menu` member actions);
- new enum members appear (`new-tab`, `separator-before`);
- new optional keys appear (`ast`, `bodyExtra`);
- `ai:chat_window` leaves the page component type unions.

On top of that, the two chained checks narrow the runtime accept set toward the spec. Hence `Clause-②: yes`. An at-tier contract review is owed before landing, as the claim already said.
